items.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: I’ve had a chance to play with him a few times, it was just unbelievable, just wonderful.

ctx.x: can’t give you a saxophone lesson in an hour and a half, but if you ask some questions, you’ll get five different answers from professionals and that will maybe give you a real idea of what your answer is and whether it’s career minded or whatever it is, music or whatever.” So somebody asked the question, “Who do you copy when you’re learning to improvise?” And I think Billy Harper says, “Well I don’t copy anybody you know. I got my own stuff” you know and everything. And then Ed Higgins says, “Well you know I…
It’s an excellent answer. Clark Terry, he has the “ations.” He says first there’s imitation, and then I think he said assimilation, and then creation of your own thing.

Well he’s one of the masters of all time. He’s just magnificent. I’ve had a chance to play with him a few times, it was just unbelievable, just wonderful. Enjoyment, fun, and a music lesson too. It’s just everything, just everything.
